item.title: 6 Best RPGs Like Chrono Trigger Worth 100% of Your Time, Ranked
item.description:
There's a reason why Chrono Trigger continues to be mentioned whenever developers talk about the RPGs that inspired them, even more than 30 years after its original release. Square's 1995 classic was ahead of its time in so many ways, particularly with its approach to combat and the way its time-traveling narrative allowed players to experience the consequences of their actions in different eras. And while the genre has evolved considerably since then, I think there's still something special about the way Chrono Trigger brought its world to life, especially when you consider just how much of its design continues to influence modern RPGs.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Thankfully, there are quite a few games that have managed to capture at least some of what made Chrono Trigger so memorable, with some developers even going so far as to acknowledge it as a direct inspiration. Of course, that doesn't necessarily mean every retro-inspired RPG is going to appeal to someone who loved the original, especially when so many of them take very different approaches to combat and storytelling. But for players who have been looking for another adventure that captures that same feeling, these six games are well worth considering.

6 I Am Setsuna

A Familiar Battle System With a Much Darker Story

Released in 2016, I Am Setsuna was developed by Tokyo RPG Factory with the intention of recreating the feeling of classic Square RPGs, and Chrono Trigger was one of its biggest influences. In fact, Square Enix specifically confirmed that the game's battle system was inspired by Chrono Trigger , which should become fairly obvious to anyone familiar with the original. It uses an Active Time Battle system that allows players to execute attacks once their gauges fill, along with combination abilities that encourage experimenting with different party members. There's also the Momentum mechanic, which rewards well-timed button presses with additional effects during combat.

Where I Am Setsuna differs most from Chrono Trigger , however, is in its story, which follows a young woman who must sacrifice herself to save her people. It's a considerably more somber experience, with its almost entirely snow-covered world giving the adventure a very different atmosphere from the colorful environments found in Chrono Trigger . I don't think that necessarily works against it, although players hoping for something with the same adventurous spirit as Square's classic might find its tone a little too melancholy. Still, the combat alone makes it worth considering, especially for those who miss the feeling of playing a traditional Square RPG.

5 Cosmic Star Heroine

One of the Closest Matches for Chrono Trigger's Combat

Cosmic Star Heroine might be one of the more overlooked games on this list, which is unfortunate considering how closely its gameplay resembles Chrono Trigger in certain areas. Developed by Zeboyd Digital Entertainment and released in 2017, it follows a secret agent named Alyssa L'Salle as she becomes caught up in a conspiracy that threatens the galaxy. The science-fiction setting gives it a considerably different identity from Chrono Trigger , but the combat should feel familiar almost immediately. In fact, developer Robert Boyd specifically cited the original game's on-map battles and multi-character combination techniques as inspirations during development.

5 SNES Masterpieces Better Than Chrono Trigger

If you think Chrono Trigger is the greatest Super Nintendo video game of all time, these masterpieces will have something to say about it.

1
By Ollie Tuscarny

But Cosmic Star Heroine also does quite a bit to distinguish itself mechanically, particularly with the way it handles abilities during combat. Rather than allowing players to repeatedly use the same powerful attacks, many abilities must be recharged before they can be used again, which encourages a more deliberate approach to battles. I actually think that's an interesting way to keep turn-based combat engaging, because it prevents players from getting too comfortable with a single strategy. And considering how much Chrono Trigger benefited from its relatively quick pacing, I appreciate that Cosmic Star Heroine places a similar emphasis on keeping the adventure moving.

4 Radiant Historia: Perfect Chronology

Time Travel Is More Than Just a Storytelling Device

For anyone who particularly enjoyed Chrono Trigger 's time-traveling narrative, I think Radiant Historia: Perfect Chronology might be one of the best alternatives available. Originally released for the Nintendo DS before receiving an expanded Nintendo 3DS version in 2018, Atlus' RPG follows Stocke, a special intelligence agent who gains the ability to travel through time using a mysterious book called the White Chronicle. Unlike Chrono Trigger , however, the game focuses on navigating alternate timelines rather than traveling between historical eras. Players can revisit important decisions and change the outcome of certain events, with progress in one timeline sometimes depending on something accomplished in another.

I particularly like the idea behind that approach, because it gives players a reason to think about how their decisions might affect events beyond the moment they're currently experiencing. Combat is also rather unique, with enemies positioned on a 3×3 grid that players can manipulate to set up powerful attacks. According to Atlus' official gameplay breakdown, players can push and pull enemies into different positions, allowing them to strike multiple targets with a single attack. It's a different kind of strategy from Chrono Trigger 's combat, but I think the game's approach to time travel is more than enough to earn it a place on this list.

3 Chained Echoes

A Modern RPG That Recaptures the SNES Era

I think one of the most impressive things about Chained Echoes is that it was developed primarily by Matthias Linda, who spent years working to create the sort of RPG he remembered playing when he was younger. Released in 2022, the game features gorgeous 16-bit-inspired pixel art and an expansive world, with its story revolving around a group of characters caught in the middle of a conflict on the continent of Valandis. There's quite a bit more to the game than its retro presentation might initially suggest, particularly once players begin exploring its world and eventually gain access to powerful mechs called Sky Armors. And as Linda confirmed in an interview with Lords of Gaming, Chrono Trigger was among the games that heavily influenced its development.

7 JRPGs With Near-Perfect Endgames, Ranked

Ready for more? These JRPG endgames bring their characters' stories and journeys to a close on a brilliant note.

By Rain Egan

What's interesting about Chained Echoes , though, is that it doesn't attempt to recreate Chrono Trigger 's combat system, instead introducing its own Overdrive mechanic. During battles, players need to manage an Overdrive gauge that affects how much damage their party deals and receives, rewarding those who can keep it within a particular range. I think that's a pretty clever way to make traditional turn-based encounters feel more involved, especially when players have to consider how their actions affect the gauge rather than simply choosing their strongest attacks. And with enemies visible throughout the world rather than appearing through random encounters, there's still plenty about Chained Echoes that should appeal to Chrono Trigger fans.

2 Chrono Cross: The Radical Dreamers Edition

Chrono Trigger's Official Follow-Up

It would be difficult to put together a list like this without mentioning Chrono Cross , especially considering it's the official follow-up to Chrono Trigger , even if it plays quite differently from its predecessor. Originally released for the PlayStation in 1999, the game follows Serge as he travels between two parallel worlds, eventually uncovering a much larger mystery involving the differences between them. Rather than bringing back Chrono Trigger 's Active Time Battle system, Chrono Cross features a stamina-based combat system and an enormous cast of more than 40 recruitable characters. It's a fairly substantial departure from the original game, which is why I wouldn't necessarily recommend it to someone who simply wants more of the same.

6 JRPGs With Virtually Perfect Progression Systems, Ranked

These JRPGs prove that character progression and complex skill systems can be just as rewarding as the adventures themselves.

By Nikol Nikolova

However, where Chrono Cross really earns its place on this list is through its narrative connections to Chrono Trigger , which become increasingly important as the story progresses. In fact, producer Koichiro Sakamoto previously explained that players who are familiar with Chrono Trigger will likely find Chrono Cross even more interesting, although it's not necessary to play the original first. The 2022 Radical Dreamers Edition also includes the previously Japan-exclusive text adventure Radical Dreamers , which helps bridge the stories of the two games. I certainly wouldn't go into Chrono Cross expecting another Chrono Trigger , but for players who want to explore more of that universe, it's arguably the most important game on this list.

1 Sea of Stars

The Best Modern Alternative to Chrono Trigger

Of all the games on this list, I think Sea of Stars comes closest to capturing the overall feeling of playing Chrono Trigger , especially when you consider how much attention Sabotage Studio put into recreating the appeal of classic RPGs. Released in 2023, the game features beautifully detailed pixel art and a traditional turn-based combat system that should feel familiar to anyone who grew up playing RPGs during the SNES era. Battles take place directly in the environment without transitioning to separate arenas, and players can execute timed inputs and combination attacks to gain an advantage over enemies. There are some important differences, though, particularly since Sea of Stars uses a fully turn-based system rather than the Active Time Battle mechanics that helped make Chrono Trigger so distinctive.

What I appreciate most about Sea of Stars is that Sabotage didn't simply set out to recreate an older RPG, but instead tried to preserve what made those games enjoyable while doing away with some of their more dated mechanics. And the connection to Chrono Trigger goes beyond the gameplay, as Yasunori Mitsuda, who composed the original game's soundtrack, contributed several original tracks to Sea of Stars as a guest composer. That involvement alone makes the game particularly interesting for Chrono Trigger fans, although I think its world and overall presentation do more than enough to justify playing it on their own. I wouldn't necessarily claim that Sea of Stars surpasses Square's 1995 classic, but if someone asked me which modern RPG they should play after finishing Chrono Trigger , this would be the one I'd recommend first.

item.title: Steam Users Have Until November 13 to Claim Turn-Based Game for Free
item.description:
Last Gambit is a 2026 turn-based game inspired by chess that is currently free on Steam , but the developer plans to charge new players around $5 USD starting November 13. Unlike Steam's usual free-to-keep promotions, which put a 100% discount on a game for a limited time, Last Gambit 's offer works differently: Players who claim it before November 13 can keep it for free, while newcomers will have to pay.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

In Last Gambit , players collect 27 chess pieces, each with unique abilities and traits that set them apart from traditional ones. These abilities and synergies let players develop unorthodox strategies on the board. For example, they can fuse pieces to create stronger ones, freeze one piece in place, or teleport another to a different tile. As developer Mads puts it, "The [chess] board is the same as always. Everything else isn't."

All The Free Games You Can Claim In November 2026

Make sure you don't miss out on a single free game in November. Epic Games Store, Amazon Prime Gaming, and Steam are a few platforms with giveaways.

By Mark Sammut

Claim Last Gambit on Steam Before It Becomes a Paid Game

Announced in a Steam Community post, Last Gambit will soon leave the roster of free games on Steam and receive a €4.99 price tag (or the regional equivalent). Developer Mads says, " If Last Gambit is in your Steam library before November 13, you keep it for free, forever ." Explaining the reasoning behind the change, the studio also said it does not want to add in-game ads or subscriptions to Last Gambit . Instead, the new price tag will help the studio sustain the game.

Last Gambit is actually a PvP and PvE game, offering several ways to experience its chess-inspired gameplay. Players can complete the campaign, which pits them against powerful AI opponents, or compete with a friend on the same device in split-screen mode. PvP matches can be played between two online players or in a 2v2 format, with two teams facing off against each other. Interestingly, when an online player declines to join a PvP match, the player who invited them can still battle their shadow, an AI-controlled opponent that uses the invited player's formation and pieces.

Two iconic game characters. One impossible mashup.
Can you name them both?

Also worth noting, Last Gambit doesn't have many user reviews on Steam at the time of writing, but the handful of comments it has received seem mostly positive. Developer Mads has also released multiple updates so far, with the 1.0 version expected to address more of the indie game's issues. And the good news is that players who claim Last Gambit for free on Steam will continue to receive updates after November 13, when the game officially exits early access.

item.title: Crimson Desert: How to Get the Pink Dolphin Legendary Mount
item.description:
While you can tame dolphins in Crimson Desert , none are as majestic and rare as the legendary Pink Dolphin! Below, we'll share the location and taming guide for the Pink Dolphin , so you know where you can find it and what you need to tame it, as this majestic creature is going to be quite the catch.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover
Crimson Desert: Golden Shark Legendary Mount Location

The Golden Shark is a Legendary Mount in Crimson Desert that can be ridden underwater! Here's where to find and tame this mighty creature.

By Jake Fillery

Make sure you bring x3 Fish Fillets and a Diving Suit, as you need to feed the Pink Dolphin. The area it spawns in is hostile, with plenty of sharks, so make a save!

How to Find & Tame the Pink Dolphin in Crimson Desert

The Pink Dolphin can be found at the Great Coral Reef, specifically just above the E" in "Great" . This location is in the very south-west area of the ocean, as noted on the map image provided above.

When you're at the Great Coral Reef, you will need to swim down regardless of the time . Once you're here, take your Diving Suit and dive to around 60 meters , where you will eventually find a herd of dolphins.

Make sure you have the Harpoon Gun. You are going to get constantly attacked by sharks that won't stop spawning, and they can one-shot kill the dolphins.

Since it's incredibly dark, it's going to be hard to spot the Pink Dolphin, so just keep mounting them until you find the one you're looking for. When you do find it, feed it three Fish Fillets from your inventory, and it will reach +100 Trust, which will allow you to register it as your mount.

The Pink Dolphin can use Underwater Detection with LB+RB (L2+R2), which allows you to scan for loot underwater. Unfortunately, the Pink Dolphin doesn't have an attack, so you'll have to defend it if a hostile creature approaches.

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake's New Wallet Creates a Classic Mystery
item.description:
When The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time first launched in 1998, there were very few things more frustrating than stumbling across a valuable Rupee when Link's wallet was already full. Of course, that was part of what made upgrading his wallet so important, especially when there were plenty of expensive items to purchase in the game. But with the upcoming Switch 2 remake increasing Link's starting wallet capacity from 99 to 200 Rupees, it seems Nintendo has decided to make carrying money a little less restrictive this time around. And while I certainly appreciate that change, it has also created a mystery surrounding one of the original game's most memorable side quests.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

What makes this particularly interesting is that Link's new starting wallet essentially gives players an upgrade they previously had to earn by collecting Gold Skulltula Tokens. In the original Ocarina of Time , players were rewarded with the Adult's Wallet after collecting 10 of those tokens, which increased their carrying capacity to 200 Rupees. But now that the remake apparently gives Link that same capacity from the beginning, I'm wondering what Nintendo has decided to do with the reward players would normally receive for completing that first milestone. And considering some of the other changes that have surfaced through early hands-on previews, I wouldn't be surprised if the Gold Skulltula quest has received a few surprises of its own.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Officially Redeems Its Worst NPC

Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is changing one of the N64 game's most infamous encounters, and a small adjustment could make a world of difference.

By Josh Cotts

Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake's New Wallet Could Change the Gold Skulltula Quest

According to Kotaku's October 14 report, which cites IGN's hands-on preview, Link can now carry up to 200 Rupees from the beginning of the Ocarina of Time remake, more than double what his original wallet allowed. That's a welcome change, especially since players can accumulate quite a bit of money simply by exploring Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field. However, the increase also means the Adult's Wallet, which was originally the first reward in the Gold Skulltula quest, no longer serves its intended purpose. Nintendo hasn't revealed what players will receive in its place, assuming that reward has been changed at all, but I think there's a pretty good opportunity here to make one of Ocarina of Time 's classic side activities even better.

For those unfamiliar with the Gold Skulltula quest, it involves collecting tokens from 100 Gold Skulltulas scattered throughout Hyrule, then returning to a cursed family in Kakariko Village to claim rewards for reaching certain milestones. The family had been transformed into spider-like creatures as punishment for their greed, and collecting the tokens gradually restored them to their human forms. Some Gold Skulltulas could only be found at night, while others were hidden behind obstacles that required Link to obtain certain items before he could reach them. To this day, I can still hear their skittering, informing me that one is nearby, ready to be killed and its token collected.

As for the rewards themselves, the Adult's Wallet was just the beginning. Collecting 20 tokens earned players the Stone of Agony, which helped locate hidden secrets when using the N64's Rumble Pak, while 30 tokens unlocked the Giant's Wallet and increased Link's capacity to 500 Rupees. The next two milestones awarded 10 Bombchus and a Piece of Heart, respectively, before collecting all 100 tokens finally freed the family's father and granted players a repeatable 200-Rupee reward. I can't say that final reward was ever particularly exciting to me, especially considering how much effort went into finding every Gold Skulltula, but Nintendo has proven time and time again that it loves torturing us with trivial rewards at the end of an exceedingly long collectathon—looking at you, Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom .

Link can now carry up to 200 Rupees from the beginning of the Ocarina of Time remake, more than double what his original wallet allowed.

Still, I'm hoping Nintendo has done something more interesting with the first reward than simply moving the Giant's Wallet down to the 10-token milestone. Sure, getting the ability to carry 500 Rupees that early would be useful, but it would also create another question about what players would receive after collecting 30 tokens. I'd much rather see something new added to the reward pool, especially if it encourages players to continue hunting Gold Skulltulas beyond those first 10. The remake has already introduced several new features and items, including an additional bottle and the ability to summon a Business Scrub merchant, so I don't think it's unreasonable to hope that Nintendo has reconsidered some of the original game's collectible rewards as well. Of course, there's no evidence yet that either of those additions is connected to the Gold Skulltula quest.

Ocarina of Time Remake Has a Chance to Make Its Classic Rewards Even Better

I also don't think giving Link a larger wallet from the beginning is necessarily taking anything important away from the original experience. The 99-Rupee limit could be frustrating at times, and with the remake introducing new ways to spend money, having a little extra room makes sense. But I do think Nintendo needs to be careful about how many of the original game's rewards it makes available without requiring players to earn them first. Part of what made exploring Ocarina of Time so satisfying was knowing that even the smallest discovery could eventually lead to something useful, and I'd hate to see some of that incentive disappear simply because Nintendo wants to make the game more convenient.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake's New Wallet Creates a Classic Mystery
Zelda's Biggest Switch 2 Launch Rival Is a Former PlayStation Hit
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Quietly Hides Easter Egg On Google
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Release Time & Early Access Guide

Ultimately, though, I'm more interested in what the remake could add to the Gold Skulltula quest than what it might have taken away. Having played the original game enough times to remember where many of those spiders are hiding, I'd love to discover that Nintendo has changed some of their locations or introduced new rewards that make collecting all 100 tokens worthwhile beyond simply completing the quest. And if the new starting wallet means the first reward has been replaced with something I haven't seen before, I think that would be a pretty good trade. There's still plenty we don't know about how extensively the remake has changed the original game, but with its November 5 release approaching, I'm looking forward to finding out whether rescuing that cursed family still has a few surprises left for me.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
